# RfcContract (rfc-contract.json)

The JSON Schema in [schemas/rfc-contract.json](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/schemas/rfc-contract.json), as a reference.

What a specification (an RFC, or markdown with numbered headings) requires of a set of functions: verbatim requirements, the functions' signatures, and the clauses (test vectors and properties) that check them. Checked against the spec text by `vector spec check`, then compiled to a test of an implementation. It names no language: it records each construct as precisely as the spec states it, and a language that cannot express one drops that detail.

| `source` | [object](#root-source) | yes | rfc alone: a single-RFC contract; `sources` may then add sources or declare rfc&lt;N&gt; itself. Or give `main` (the source the completeness gate reads) and `sources` instead of rfc. |
| `sources` | [`sourceDecl`](#def-sourcedecl)[] | no | The documents the contract cites, by id. Citations name one with `source` (default: the main one). at least 1 items. |

No other property is allowed.

## Definitions

<a id="def-id"></a>

### `id`

`string`; matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`.

<a id="def-section"></a>

### `section`

A section number: 2.3, A.1, 4 (an RFC's, or a markdown spec's numbered heading).

`string`; matches `^(?:\d+(?:\.\d+)*|[A-Z](?:\.\d+)*)$`.

<a id="def-modulepath"></a>

### `modulePath`

A module as a neutral path `<root>/<segment>/…`: lowercase segments separated by `/`, like the segments of a URI path (RFC 3986 §3.3).

`string`; matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(?:/[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$`.

<a id="def-moduleoverrides"></a>

### `moduleOverrides`

Per-language override of the module form, keyed by language: how that language names the module when its default form, derived from the neutral path, is wrong. A language not listed uses its default.

<a id="def-ident"></a>

### `ident`

`string`; matches `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`.

<a id="def-inttype"></a>

### `intType`

A fixed-width integer: iN is two's complement and uN unsigned, N bits wide, as ISO C11 §7.20.1.1 intN_t/uintN_t; + - * wrap modulo 2^N.

`"i8"` \| `"i16"` \| `"i32"` \| `"i64"` \| `"u8"` \| `"u16"` \| `"u32"` \| `"u64"`

<a id="def-intvalue"></a>

### `intValue`

An integer: a JSON integer within ±(2^53−1), or a decimal string for a value beyond it, so 64-bit values are exact (RFC 7493 §2.2, RFC 8259 §6). The string must not be a value a JSON integer could carry; its pattern admits only 16 digits or more, since the exact bound 2^53−1 is beyond a pattern and is the contract validator's to check.

One or more of:

- `integer` (at least -9007199254740991; at most 9007199254740991)
- `string` (matches `^-?[1-9][0-9]{15,}$`)

<a id="def-f64text"></a>

### `f64Text`

An IEEE 754-2019 binary64 value as text: a decimal, converted to the nearest double with roundTiesToEven (§4.3.1, §5.12.2), or NaN, Infinity, -Infinity; -0 is negative zero.

`string`; matches `^(?:-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?|NaN|Infinity|-Infinity)$`.

<a id="def-f64bound"></a>

### `f64Bound`

An f64Text that is not NaN, for a bound of an f64 domain: NaN is unordered (IEEE 754-2019 §5.11), so it bounds nothing.

`string`; matches `^(?:-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?|Infinity|-Infinity)$`.

<a id="def-f64bits"></a>

### `f64Bits`

The IEEE 754-2019 binary64 encoding (§3.4) as 16 lowercase hex digits, most significant first; it is how a NaN's payload is stated, and NaN compares by these bits.

`string`; matches `^[0-9a-f]{16}$`.

<a id="def-paramtype"></a>

### `paramType`

A parameter's type. bytes is an octet string; string is Unicode text, UTF-8 encoded (RFC 3629); f64 is an IEEE 754-2019 binary64; i8 … u64 are the fixed-width integers (see intType); secret-bytes is bytes whose value is secret: a language may wrap them in its own secret type, but in the contract they are bytes. T? as a parameter is an optional input: the argument may be absent, written null.

`"bytes"` \| `"bytes?"` \| `"string"` \| `"string?"` \| `"bool"` \| `"bool?"` \| `"f64"` \| `"f64?"` \| `"secret-bytes"` \| `"secret-bytes?"` \| `"i8"` \| `"i8?"` \| `"i16"` \| `"i16?"` \| `"i32"` \| `"i32?"` \| `"i64"` \| `"i64?"` \| `"u8"` \| `"u8?"` \| `"u16"` \| `"u16?"` \| `"u32"` \| `"u32?"` \| `"u64"` \| `"u64?"`

<a id="def-returntype"></a>

### `returnType`

A result's type, from the types of paramType. T? as a result is a refusing return: the function declines this input and returns no value, written null.

`"bytes"` \| `"bytes?"` \| `"string"` \| `"string?"` \| `"bool"` \| `"bool?"` \| `"f64"` \| `"f64?"` \| `"secret-bytes"` \| `"secret-bytes?"` \| `"i8"` \| `"i8?"` \| `"i16"` \| `"i16?"` \| `"i32"` \| `"i32?"` \| `"i64"` \| `"i64?"` \| `"u8"` \| `"u8?"` \| `"u16"` \| `"u16?"` \| `"u32"` \| `"u32?"` \| `"u64"` \| `"u64?"`

One or more of:

(null when any byte &gt;= 0x80); charAt(string,i32)-&gt;string ("" out of range); unwrap/isNull/notNull also take string?; == != also on string/string?/null.

<a id="def-vectorclause"></a>

### `vectorClause`

A known answer: call(args) == expect. The args are printed in the cited section (with a cite source) or in `section`; `source` says where the expected value comes from.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"vector"` | yes |  |
| `id` | [`id`](#def-id) | yes |  |
| `title` | `string` | yes |  |
| `covers` | [`id`](#def-id)[] | yes | at least 1 items. |
| `source` | [`vectorSource`](#def-vectorsource) | yes |  |
| `section` | [`section`](#def-section) | no | Only with a command or spec source: the main-source section printing the args. |
| `call` | `string` | yes |  |
| `args` | [`literal`](#def-literal)[] | yes |  |
| `expect` | [`literal`](#def-literal) | yes |  |
| `tolerance` | [`tolerance`](#def-tolerance) | no |  |
| `iterate` | [`iterate`](#def-iterate) | no |  |
| `truncate` | [`truncate`](#def-truncate) | no |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-propertyclause"></a>

### `propertyClause`

For all inputs in the domain (and `where`), `assert` holds. Z3 picks boundary samples; a seeded PRNG adds random ones.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"property"` | yes |  |
| `id` | [`id`](#def-id) | yes |  |
| `title` | `string` | yes |  |
| `covers` | [`id`](#def-id)[] | yes | at least 1 items. |
| `forall` | [object[]](#def-propertyclause-forall-variant-1) | yes |  |
| `where` | [`expr`](#def-expr) | no | Pure (no calls): restricts the domain. |
| `assert` | [`expr`](#def-expr) | yes |  |
| `samples` | `integer` | no | The property's total samples, Z3's boundaries first (at most this many) then seeded random draws until it has this many. Absent: every boundary plus 24 random, at most 96 in all. at least 1; at most 256. |

No other property is allowed.

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-sourcedecl"></a>

### `sourceDecl`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | [`id`](#def-id) | yes |  |
| `rfc` | `integer` | no | An RFC number. Unless `path` is given, its text is rfc&lt;N&gt;.xml, else rfc&lt;N&gt;.txt, beside the contract, in ../rfcs, then in vector's rfcs/; at each place the XML comes first, and a recorded `file` picks between them. |
| `path` | `string` | no | The spec's file, relative to the contract. |
| `file` | `string` | no | The file whose bytes were read for this source: its path under rfcs/ or specs/ of the nearest directory holding it there, counting the contract's directory, its ancestors and vector's own root (e.g. rfcs/rfc4648.txt), or, for a file beside the contract, from the directory holding the contract's directory (contracts/x.txt). `vector spec check` fails when it reads another file. |
| `sha256` | `string` | no | The sha256 of that file's bytes. `vector spec check` and `vector spec frozen` fail when the bytes differ. matches `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`. |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-citation"></a>

### `citation`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | [`id`](#def-id) | no | The id of the cited source (default: the main one). |
| `section` | [`section`](#def-section) | yes |  |
| `case` | `string` | no | One test case of the section, as `Test Vector #N`: the vector's labelled values are read from that case alone, from its `Test Vector #N:` heading to the next. Absent for the whole section. matches `^Test Vector #[1-9][0-9]{0,5}$`. |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-vectorsource"></a>

### `vectorSource`

Where the expected value comes from: printed in a cited section; the stdout of a command (run under --run-sources); or, for an expected null or bool, a section that states it.

One or more of:

- [an object `variant 1`](#def-vectorsource-variant-1)
- [an object `variant 2`](#def-vectorsource-variant-2)
- [an object `variant 3`](#def-vectorsource-variant-3)

<a id="def-vectorsource-variant-1"></a>

#### `variant 1`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cite` | [`citation`](#def-citation) | yes |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-vectorsource-variant-2"></a>

#### `variant 2`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | `string` | yes |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-vectorsource-variant-3"></a>

#### `variant 3`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spec` | [`section`](#def-section) | yes |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-label"></a>

### `label`

The name the spec prints right before the value (`Key = 00:01:…`, `L = 42`); fidelity checks the pair.

`string`; matches `[A-Za-z]`; at least 1 characters.

<a id="def-iterate"></a>

### `iterate`

Feed the call its own result `count` times: the first call takes `args`; each later call takes `next`, where a name is that parameter's previous argument and the element `{call, args: names}` is the previous call's result. The vector passes when the last result equals `expect`. `names` and `next` are one per parameter of `call`; each element's type must equal its parameter's (`bytes` and `secret-bytes` interchange, and a nullable result feeds its base type); at least one element is the call. The count must be printed in the cited section (commas ignored), and when the expect's label holds a number it must be the count. Not with `tolerance`, nor on a null or bool expect. `slow` marks a vector a test runs only when asked; it is written only when true.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `integer` | yes | at least 1; at most 1000000000. |
| `names` | [`ident`](#def-ident)[] | yes | at least 1 items. |
| `next` | [object[]](#def-iterate-next-variant-1) | yes | at least 1 items. |
| `slow` | `boolean` | no |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-iterate-next-variant-1"></a>

#### `next[] (variant 1)`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `var` | [`ident`](#def-ident) | yes |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-iterate-next-variant-2"></a>

#### `next[] (variant 2)`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `call` | `string` | yes |  |
| `args` | [object[]](#def-iterate-next-variant-2-args) | yes |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-iterate-next-variant-2-args"></a>

#### `next[] (variant 2).args[]`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `var` | [`ident`](#def-ident) | yes |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-truncate"></a>

### `truncate`

Hold only the first bytes of the call's result to `expect`, as a spec does when it prints a result truncated (RFC 4231 §4.6: "Truncate to 128 bits"). Exactly one of `bits`, a multiple of 8, or `bytes` gives the length, written in the unit the spec prints. The call returns bytes, `expect` is bytes of exactly that length, and a result shorter than the length fails the check rather than being compared as it is. The length must be printed in the cited section with its unit (commas ignored). Not with `tolerance` or `iterate`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bits` | `integer` | no | at least 8; at most 524288. |
| `bytes` | `integer` | no | at least 1; at most 65536. |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-tolerance"></a>

### `tolerance`

How far an f64 result may be from `expect`: `abs`, an absolute difference as decimal text, or `ulps`, a count of binary64 units in the last place. It must come from the spec: `quote` is the sentence that states it, in `section` (of `source`, default the main one), checked like a requirement's quote. Without a tolerance an f64 expect is compared bit for bit (IEEE 754-2019 §3.4 encodings), so NaN equals a NaN of the same bits. Only an f64 result takes a tolerance, and an expected NaN or infinity is compared bit for bit even with one. `abs` must be finite: decimal text past binary64's largest finite value is refused (IEEE 754-2019 §7.4). `ulps` is at most 2^53−1, so it is exact as a JSON number (RFC 7493 §2.2).

One or more of:

- [an object `variant 1`](#def-tolerance-variant-1)
- [an object `variant 2`](#def-tolerance-variant-2)

<a id="def-tolerance-variant-1"></a>

#### `variant 1`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `abs` | `string` | yes | matches `^(?:0\|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?$`. |
| `source` | [`id`](#def-id) | no |  |
| `section` | [`section`](#def-section) | yes |  |
| `quote` | `string` | yes | at least 1 characters. |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-tolerance-variant-2"></a>

#### `variant 2`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ulps` | `integer` | yes | at least 0; at most 9007199254740991. |
| `source` | [`id`](#def-id) | no |  |
| `section` | [`section`](#def-section) | yes |  |
| `quote` | `string` | yes | at least 1 characters. |

No other property is allowed.
